mainTopic: The reward for אברהם's refusal of the spoils, teachings on humility, and whether dust of an עיר הנדחת may be used for כיסוי הדם (מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו).
overview: The amud opens with a reward for אברהם. He refused even 'a thread or a shoe strap' from the king of סדום, so his children received the thread of תכלת and the strap of תפילין. רבי מאיר explains that תכלת's color leads the mind to the כסא הכבוד. רבי אבא learns from the same story that stolen food that was eaten is very hard to return. The גמרא then gathers teachings on humility. ה׳ loves ישראל because its great leaders, אברהם, משה and אהרן, and דוד, made themselves small, while the nations' rulers grew proud. Several sages teach that the world stands in the merit of the humble, and רבי יצחק says a person should stay silent except for words of Torah, without becoming proud. The גמרא then returns to כיסוי הדם. רבי זעירא allows covering the blood with dust of an עיר הנדחת. זעירי explains that he means ground dust that was never forbidden, and רבא says doing a מצוה is not 'benefit'. Challenges from a שופר and a לולב of עבודה זרה lead to רב אשי's answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two מצוות as a reward for refusing a thread and a strap
steps.stepSummary: Because אברהם refused even a thread or a shoe strap from the king of סדום, his children were rewarded with the thread of תכלת and the strap of תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because אברהם said 'not even a thread or a shoe strap,' his children earned two מצוות: the thread of תכלת and the strap of תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that אברהם's refusal to take even a thread or a shoe strap was rewarded with two matching מצוות for his children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reward matches the words אברהם used. He said 'thread,' so his children got the thread of תכלת on ציצית. He said 'shoe strap,' so they got the strap of תפילין.

keyTerms.meaning: a shoe strap or lace
they earned or merited
the sky-blue thread in ציצית
the leather strap of תפילין

phrases.english: "Not even a thread or a shoe strap"
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:23. This is אברהם speaking to the king of סדום, refusing to keep any of the spoils.

phrases.english: his children merited two מצוות:
the thread of sky-blue wool,
and the strap of tefillin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the teaching (from before this section) about the reward אברהם received for refusing the spoils of סדום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The reward for refusing 'a thread and a shoe strap' was the thread of תכלת and the strap of תפילין.

steps.title: What is special about the thread of תכלת?
steps.stepSummary: The strap of תפילין is clearly a reward, because a פסוק says the nations see ה׳'s name on us through the head תפילין. But what makes the תכלת thread a reward?
steps.simpleTranslation: We understand the strap of תפילין. The פסוק says 'All the nations will see that ה׳'s name is called on you,' and רבי אליעזר הגדול says this means the head תפילין. But what is so special about the thread of תכלת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts that תפילין are a fitting reward. It asks what is so great about the תכלת thread. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A reward should bring honor. The head תפילין bring honor because they show ה׳'s name on a Jew, as a פסוק and a ברייתא prove. The תכלת thread has no such obvious source, so the גמרא asks what it adds.

keyTerms.meaning: granted, this part makes sense (but the next part is hard)
the תפילין worn on the head
but (introduces the part that is hard)
what is it? (what is special about it)

phrases.english: Granted, the strap of tefillin,
it is written: "And all the peoples of the earth will see
phrases.notes: דברים 28:10.

phrases.english: that the name of ה׳ is called upon you,"
and it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
this refers to the tefillin of the head,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חוּט שֶׁל תְּכֵלֶת מַאי הִיא?
phrases.english: but the thread of sky-blue wool, what is it?
phrases.notes: He means: what is special or honorable about it that makes it a reward?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for an explanation of the second reward named in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the thread of תכלת counts as an honorable reward, the way the head תפילין do.

steps.title: תכלת reminds us of the כסא הכבוד
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר teaches that תכלת's color leads step by step to the כסא הכבוד: the sea, the sky, sapphire stone, and finally the Throne. Two פסוקים prove the links.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Why is תכלת different from all other colors? Because תכלת looks like the sea, the sea looks like the sky, the sky looks like sapphire stone, and sapphire stone looks like the כסא הכבוד. Two פסוקים show this. One says 'They saw the God of Israel, and under His feet...' and the other says 'like the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא of רבי מאיר. The color of תכלת reminds a person of ה׳'s כסא הכבוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the head תפילין, תכלת connects the Jew to ה׳, so it is a fitting reward. The chain goes: thread, sea, sky, sapphire, Throne. The first פסוק links the sky to sapphire. The second links sapphire to the Throne.

keyTerms.meaning: colors or dyes
the sky, the heavens
sapphire stone
ה׳'s Throne of Glory

steps.whatToRemember: תכלת is a fitting reward because its color leads the mind step by step to the כסא הכבוד, just as תפילין show ה׳'s name on us.

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Meir says:
What is different about sky-blue from all other colors?
Because sky-blue is similar to the sea,
and the sea is similar to the sky,
and the sky is similar to sapphire stone,
and sapphire stone is similar to the Throne of Glory,
as it is written: "And they saw the God of Israel,
phrases.notes: שמות 24:10.

phrases.english: and under His feet, etc."
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק describes sapphire stone that looks like the sky, which links the sky to sapphire.

phrases.english: and it is written: "Like the appearance of sapphire stone, the likeness of a throne."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 1:26.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תכלת's color leads by a chain of likeness to the כסא הכבוד, so it connects the Jew to ה׳.

steps.title: Stolen food that was eaten is hard to return
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא learns from אברהם's words 'except what the young men have eaten' that stolen food already eaten is very hard to return, even for complete צדיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: Stolen food that was eaten is a serious problem, because even complete צדיקים cannot return it. As the פסוק says: 'Except only what the young men have eaten.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from the same story. רבי אבא says it is very hard to return stolen things that were already eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם returned everything to the king of סדום. He could not return the food his young men had already eaten. If even אברהם, a complete צדיק, could not return it, then eaten stolen goods are especially hard to fix.

keyTerms.meaning: stolen property that was eaten
completely righteous people
to return it
apart from me, except

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that once stolen food is eaten, it cannot simply be handed back, so the wrong is much harder to fix.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: קָשֶׁה גָּזֵל הַנֶּאֱכָל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said: Difficult is stolen property that has been eaten,
for even completely righteous people
are not able to return it,
as it is said: "Except only what the young men have eaten."
phrases.notes: בראשית 14:24. אברהם gave everything back, except the food his men had already eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: קָשֶׁה גָּזֵל הַנֶּאֱכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story of אברהם and the spoils of סדום from step 1 to draw a new lesson.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stolen food that was eaten is so hard to return that even complete צדיקים cannot do it.

steps.title: Listen closely to the aggadic teachings of רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון, says to pay close attention to the הגדה of רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון: Wherever you find the words of רבי אליעזר, son of רבי יוסי הגלילי, in הגדה, make your ears like a funnel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic with an introduction. It praises a certain sage's aggadic teachings, and this sets up the teaching of his that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No law or teaching is given yet. The line tells us how seriously to take what follows. A funnel takes in everything poured into it, so we should take in all of his words.

keyTerms.meaning: The non-legal parts of Torah teaching: stories, lessons, and explanations of פסוקים
A funnel. Here it means: be fully open to taking in his words
In the name of. Used when a sage passes on a teaching he heard from someone else

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon:
Any place where you find

phrases.aramaic: דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
in aggada,
make your ears like a funnel.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁאַתָּה מוֹצֵא דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי בַּהַגָּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new aggadic topic. It is loosely connected to the earlier steps about אברהם's greatness and character.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The aggadic teachings of רבי אליעזר בנו של רבי יוסי הגלילי deserve full and careful attention.

steps.title: ה׳ loves ישראל because they stay humble when given greatness
steps.stepSummary: Reading the פסוק 'לא מרבכם‎', ה׳ tells ישראל that He loves them because they make themselves small even when He makes them great.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Not because you are more numerous than all the nations did ה׳ desire you.' ה׳ said to ישראל: I desire you because even when I give you greatness, you make yourselves small before Me.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the teaching of רבי אליעזר that the last step introduced. He explains why ה׳ chose ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ה׳ did not choose ישראל because they were many. The teaching explains the real reason: they make themselves small. This is especially true when they are given greatness, which is when a person is most tempted to become proud.

keyTerms.meaning: Desired, loved deeply
Giving greatness generously
You make yourselves small, meaning you act humbly

steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ loves ישראל because they answer greatness with humility.

phrases.english: "Not because you are more numerous than all the nations
phrases.notes: דברים 7:7

phrases.english: did ה׳ desire you, etc."

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the Jewish people:
I desire you,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁאֲנִי מַשְׁפִּיעַ לָכֶם גְּדוּלָּה –
phrases.english: since even at a time when I give you greatness,
you make yourselves small before Me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶם הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל: חוֹשְׁקַנִי בָּכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual teaching of the sage praised in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ישראל is beloved because its people humble themselves even when they are given greatness.

steps.title: Examples of Jewish leaders who humbled themselves
steps.stepSummary: אברהם, משה and אהרן, and דוד were each given greatness, and each one described himself as lowly.
steps.simpleTranslation: I gave greatness to אברהם, and he said before Me: 'I am dust and ashes.' To משה and אהרן, and he said: 'What are we?' To דוד, and he said: 'I am a worm and not a man.'
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳'s words go on with examples that prove the claim in step 6. Each great Jewish leader answered greatness by calling himself small.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each example follows the same pattern: ה׳ gave greatness, and the person answered with humble words. Each example is backed by a פסוק. These cases turn the general claim of step 6 into something we can see.

keyTerms.meaning: Dust and ashes, said by אברהם
And what are we? Said by משה about himself and אהרן
A worm and not a man, said by דוד

phrases.english: I gave greatness to Abraham,
yet he said before Me: "I am dust and ashes";
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:27

phrases.english: to Moses and Aaron, yet he said: "And what are we";
phrases.notes: שמות 16:7. משה said this about both himself and אהרן.

phrases.english: to David, yet he said: "But I am a worm and not a man."
phrases.notes: תהלים 22:7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives examples that prove the claim of step 6.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that ישראל humbles itself when given greatness
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים quoting אברהם, משה, and דוד describing themselves as lowly

steps.title: In contrast, the nations' rulers became arrogant when given greatness
steps.stepSummary: נמרוד, פרעה, סנחריב, נבוכדנצר, and חירם king of צור were given greatness, and each became proud and challenged ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the nations of the world are not like this. I gave greatness to נמרוד, and he said: 'Let us build a city.' To פרעה, and he said: 'Who is ה׳?' To סנחריב, and he said: 'Who among all the gods of the lands.' To נבוכדנצר, and he said: 'I will rise above the clouds.' To חירם king of צור, and he said: 'I sit in the seat of God in the heart of the seas.'
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳'s words now show the opposite side. Non-Jewish rulers were also given greatness, but they answered it with arrogance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as in step 7: greatness was given, and the person answered. This time, though, the answer is pride instead of humility. The contrast makes clear what is special about ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: The nations of the world, meaning non-Jewish peoples
The heights of the clouds
In the heart of the seas

steps.whatToRemember: When given the same greatness, ישראל's leaders made themselves small, while the nations' rulers made themselves into gods.

phrases.english: But the nations of the world are not like this.
I gave greatness to Nimrod,
yet he said: "Come, let us build ourselves a city";
phrases.notes: בראשית 11:4. This is the tower of בבל, whose top would reach the heavens.

phrases.english: to Pharaoh, yet he said: "Who is ה׳";
phrases.notes: שמות 5:2

phrases.english: to Sennacherib, yet he said:
"Who among all the gods of the lands, etc.";
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 18:35

phrases.english: to Nebuchadnezzar, yet he said: "I will rise above the heights of the clouds";
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 14:14

phrases.english: to Hiram king of Tyre, yet he said:
"I sit in the seat of God, in the heart of the seas."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 28:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of step 7's examples, to show how ישראל is different.
steps.raayaSupportSource: פסוקים quoting the proud words of five non-Jewish rulers

steps.title: The humility of משה and אהרן was greater than that of אברהם
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יוחנן) compares the two humble statements. אברהם called himself dust and ashes, but משה and אהרן said 'what are we?', as if they were nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said, and some say רבי יוחנן: What is said about משה and אהרן is greater than what is said about אברהם. About אברהם it is written 'I am dust and ashes', but about משה and אהרן it is written 'And what are we?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new sage now compares two of the examples from step 7. He says that משה and אהרן's humility goes further than אברהם's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם said he was something lowly, dust and ashes, but that is still something. משה and אהרן said 'what are we?', meaning they are not even that. So the second statement shows a deeper humility.

keyTerms.meaning: For whereas. It starts a comparison between two cases

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yochanan said:
Greater is what is said about Moses and Aaron
than what is said about Abraham.
For about Abraham it is written: "I am dust and ashes,"
while about Moses and Aaron it is written: "And what are we."

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּדוֹל שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר בְּאַבְרָהָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares two of the examples from step 7 against each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The humility of משה and אהרן, who called themselves nothing, is greater than that of אברהם, who called himself dust and ashes.

steps.title: The world stands because of משה and אהרן
steps.stepSummary: רבא (or רבי יוחנן) links 'ונחנו מה' to the פסוק 'תולה ארץ על בלימה' and teaches that the world exists in the merit of משה and אהרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said, and some say רבי יוחנן: The world only exists because of משה and אהרן. Here it is written 'And what are we', and there it is written 'He hangs the earth upon nothing.'
steps.whatsHappening: The same sage adds a second teaching about משה and אהרן. Their humility is what holds up the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from a shared word. משה and אהרן said 'מה', and the earth hangs on 'בלימה', which can be read as 'without anything'. So the earth rests on the people who saw themselves as nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Exists, keeps going
It is written here, and it is written there. This links two פסוקים through a shared word
Nothingness, read here as 'בלי מה', without anything

steps.whatToRemember: Humility is so powerful that the world stands in the merit of משה and אהרן, who saw themselves as nothing.
steps.confusionAlert: The world's existence is not tied to how great משה and אהרן were. It is tied to how small they made themselves, the 'מה' that appears again in 'בלימה'.

phrases.english: And Rava said, and some say Rabbi Yochanan said:
The world does not exist
except because of Moses and Aaron.
It is written here: "And what are we,"
and it is written there: "He hangs the earth upon nothing."
phrases.notes: איוב 26:7. Read בלימה as בלי מה, 'without anything', which uses the same word מה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין הָעוֹלָם מִתְקַיֵּים אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching by the same sage, building on 'ונחנו מה' from step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world exists in the merit of משה and אהרן, learned from the link between 'מה' and 'בלימה'.

steps.title: The world stands on one who holds himself back in a fight
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא reads בלימה as 'holding back': the world exists in the merit of someone who keeps quiet during an argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא said: The world only lasts because of the person who holds himself back during a fight, as the פסוק says, 'He hangs the earth upon בלימה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא gives a second reading of the same פסוק from Step 10, 'תולה ארץ על בלימה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 10 בלימה meant 'nothing', pointing to משה and אהרן who saw themselves as nothing. רבי אילעא hears בלימה as coming from בולם, to restrain. So the world rests on anyone who can stop himself from fighting back in an argument.

keyTerms.meaning: Restrains himself, holds himself back
A quarrel, a fight

phrases.english: Rabbi Ile'a said:
The world does not endure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבִיל מִי שֶׁבּוֹלֵם אֶת עַצְמוֹ
phrases.english: except for the sake of one who restrains himself
at the time of a quarrel,
as it is stated: "He hangs the earth upon nothing."
phrases.notes: איוב 26:7. He hears בלימה like בולם, so it means 'holding back'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the same פסוק used in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world exists in the merit of one who restrains himself during a quarrel.

steps.title: The world stands on one who sees himself as nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says the world exists in the merit of one who makes himself as if he is not there, and he learns it from a different פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו says: The world lasts because of the person who treats himself as if he does not exist, as the פסוק says, 'And underneath are the everlasting arms.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives his own view of whose merit holds up the world, using a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'ומתחת זרועות עולם' as 'the one who places himself underneath everyone is the arm that holds up the world.' His focus is on total self-lowering in general, not only staying quiet during a fight.

keyTerms.meaning: Treats himself as if he does not exist
The everlasting arms that hold up the world

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu says:
(It is in the merit of) one who makes himself as if he does not exist,
phrases.notes: He is finishing רבי אילעא's sentence: 'the world only lasts because of...'

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And underneath are the everlasting arms."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:27

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion beside רבי אילעא about whose merit sustains the world.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The world exists in the merit of one who considers himself as nothing.

steps.title: Be silent, but speak Torah and stay humble
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק reads a פסוק in תהלים as a guide: a person's job is to be quiet like a mute, but not about Torah, and even Torah learning must not make him proud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: What does the פסוק 'Do you indeed speak as a righteous company? Do you judge the sons of men with fairness?' mean? A person's job in this world is to make himself like a mute. You might think this applies even to Torah, so the פסוק says 'speak righteousness.' You might think he may then become proud, so the פסוק says 'judge people fairly.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק explains a פסוק by playing on its words, and each part of the פסוק adds a new limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads האמנם as אומנות (a job) and אלם as אילם (a mute), so the main lesson is to stay quiet. Then 'צדק תדברון' makes an exception: you must speak words of Torah. Last, 'מישרים תשפטו' stops the Torah speaker from getting arrogant, so he must still judge carefully and fairly.

keyTerms.meaning: A craft, a job, one's occupation
A mute, someone who does not speak
'You might think...', which brings up a possible mistake
'The פסוק teaches', which answers that mistake
Becomes proud, arrogant

steps.whatToRemember: Silence is a person's main job, but Torah must be spoken, and speaking Torah must not lead to pride.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said: What is the meaning of what is written:
"Do you indeed speak as a righteous company?
phrases.notes: תהלים 58:2. He reads האמנם as 'job' and אלם as 'a mute'.

phrases.english: Do you judge the sons of men with fairness?"

phrases.aramaic: מָה אוּמָּנוּתוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה –
phrases.english: What is a person's job in this world?
He should make himself like a mute.
You might think: even about words of Torah?
The verse teaches: "Speak righteousness."
You might think he may become proud?
The verse teaches: "Judge the sons of men with fairness."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of humility with a new פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person should keep silent, except for Torah, and must not grow proud from it.

steps.title: Covering blood with dust of an עיר הנדחת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to כיסוי הדם. רבי זעירא rules that you may cover the blood with dust from an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זעירא said, and some say it was רבה בר ירמיה: We may cover the blood with the dust of an עיר הנדחת.
steps.whatsHappening: The humility section is over, and the גמרא returns to its main topic, covering the blood of a חיה or bird. A new rule is stated, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עיר הנדחת is a city that turned to עבודה זרה. The Torah says it must be burned and nothing from it may be used. So saying its dust may be used for a מצוה is surprising, and the גמרא will ask about it next.

keyTerms.meaning: We cover (the blood, for the מצוה of כיסוי הדם)
A city whose people turned to עבודה זרה; it must be burned

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said, and some say Rabba bar Yirmeya:
We may cover with the dust of an idolatrous city.
phrases.notes: We're back to covering the blood of a חיה or bird after שחיטה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זְעֵירָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and returns to the laws of כיסוי הדם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood may be covered with the dust of an עיר הנדחת.

steps.title: But benefit from it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this dust can be used, since everything from an עיר הנדחת is אסור בהנאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? It is something you are not allowed to benefit from!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זעירא's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes רבי זעירא means the ashes left after the city is burned. Those ashes are אסורי הנאה, and using them to do a מצוה counts as getting benefit from them. So how could they be allowed?

keyTerms.meaning: 'But why?', which opens a challenge
Things you may not get any benefit or use from

phrases.english: But why?
It is something forbidden for benefit!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is thinking of the ashes left after the city is burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule just stated.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זעירא's rule that the dust of an עיר הנדחת may be used for covering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Everything from an עיר הנדחת is אסור בהנאה, and covering blood with it is a benefit.

steps.title: He means the city's own ground dust
steps.stepSummary: זעירי answers that רבי זעירא meant the dust of the ground itself. The פסוק only forbids things that just need gathering and burning, not ground that would first have to be dug up.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: The rule is only needed for the dust of the ground itself, as it says, 'And you shall gather all its spoil into its open square and burn.' That means things that only still need gathering and burning. That leaves out this ground dust, which would still need to be dug up, gathered, and burned.
steps.whatsHappening: זעירי answers the challenge by explaining which dust רבי זעירא was talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes of the burned city really are forbidden. But the פסוק only covers 'spoil' that just needs to be gathered and burned. Ground dust is attached to the earth and would first need to be pulled up, so it is not part of the forbidden spoil and may be used for covering.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was only needed for...', which narrows a rule to a specific case
The dust of its dust: the city's own ground soil
Its spoil, the movable things of the city
Lacking, still needing (an action)
Detaching, pulling up from the ground

steps.whatToRemember: The ashes of an עיר הנדחת are forbidden, but its ground dust is not, because the Torah only forbids what needs just gathering and burning.
steps.confusionAlert: According to זעירי, רבי זעירא is not allowing the burned ashes of the city. Those stay forbidden, and he only allows the plain ground dust. רבא in the next step says even the ashes may be used.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
It was needed only for the dust of its dust,
phrases.notes: He means the city's own ground soil, not the burned ashes.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And all its spoil
you shall gather into the midst of its open square, and you shall burn,"
phrases.notes: דברים 13:17

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְחוּסָּר אֶלָּא קְבִיצָה וּשְׂרֵפָה,
phrases.english: meaning something that lacks only gathering and burning,

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁמְחוּסָּר תְּלִישָׁה, קְבִיצָה וּשְׂרֵפָה.
phrases.english: which leaves out this, which lacks detaching, gathering, and burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר זְעֵירִי: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לַעֲפַר עֲפָרָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 15 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זעירא meant the forbidden ashes of the burned city.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant the ground dust, which is not part of the forbidden spoil because it still needs detaching.

steps.title: רבא: Doing a מצוה is not called getting benefit
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer to the question of how the dust of an עיר הנדחת can be used: doing a מצוה is not treated as getting benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: מצוות were not given to give benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question from step 15 in a new way. He says the dust may be used because using something for a מצוה does not count as enjoying it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי solved the problem by saying the ground dust was never forbidden. רבא says that even if the item is אסור בהנאה, covering the blood is not 'benefit', because a מצוה is a command from הקב״ה and not a personal pleasure. So the איסור הנאה never comes into play.

keyTerms.meaning: מצוות were not given for benefit, so doing a מצוה with something does not count as enjoying it

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for the dust of an עיר הנדחת: זעירי says ground dust was never forbidden, and רבא says doing a מצוה is not 'benefit'.
steps.whyThisMatters: מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו is a famous rule that comes up in many places in ש״ס, whenever someone wants to do a מצוה with a forbidden item.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
מצוות were not given for benefit.
phrases.notes: He means that covering the blood with forbidden dust is not counted as 'using' it for your own enjoyment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the קשיא of step 15, in place of זעירי's answer in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the problem: the action is not 'benefit' at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Using dust from an עיר הנדחת to cover blood is forbidden benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Doing a מצוה is not benefit, so even forbidden items may be used for it.

steps.title: Challenge from a שופר of עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: While רבינא is teaching רבא's rule, רב רחומי challenges it from a ברייתא that says you may not blow a שופר of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא was sitting and teaching this teaching. רב רחומי challenged רבינא: 'A שופר of עבודה זרה, one may not blow with it.' Doesn't that mean that if he blew, he was not יוצא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב רחומי attacks רבא's rule. He brings a ברייתא that says not to blow a שופר of עבודה זרה, and suggests this means the מצוה does not even count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מצוה is not 'benefit', then a forbidden שופר should work just fine. But the ברייתא says not to blow with it. רב רחומי reads this as 'if he blew, he did not do the מצוה', which would show that a forbidden item does not work for a מצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or ruling
Idol worship; its items are אסור בהנאה
'Doesn't it mean...?' A way of suggesting how to read a source
He did not fulfill his obligation

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רָבִינָא וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא,
phrases.english: Ravina was sitting and saying this teaching,
phrases.notes: This is רבא's rule from the last step, that מצוות are not 'benefit'.

phrases.english: Rav Rechumi challenged Ravina:
A shofar of idol worship,
one should not blow with it.
Doesn't it mean,
that if he blew, he did not fulfill his obligation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's rule from step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a forbidden שופר does not work for the מצוה, then using a forbidden item for a מצוה must be a problem, against רבא.

steps.title: Answer: only not at the start, but it counts after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא only means you should not blow it at the start, but if you did, you were יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means that if he blew, he was יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב רחומי's reading. The ברייתא only says not to use it at the start; after the fact, the מצוה counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between 'you should not' and 'it does not count'. Reading the ברייתא as only לכתחילה keeps רבא's rule safe, because after the fact the מצוה still works.

keyTerms.meaning: He fulfilled his obligation
At the start (before acting) / after the fact (once it was done)

steps.confusionAlert: 'He should not blow' does not always mean 'it doesn't count'. Often it only means 'don't do it at the start'.

phrases.english: No,
if he blew, he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source as לכתחילה only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Should not blow' means the מצוה does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Should not blow' only means not at the start; after the fact he is יוצא.

steps.title: Second challenge from a לולב of עבודה זרה
steps.stepSummary: רב רחומי brings the same kind of challenge from a לולב of עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A לולב of עבודה זרה, one may not take it.' Doesn't that mean that if he took it, he was not יוצא?
steps.whatsHappening: רב רחומי tries again with a second case from the ברייתא, a לולב of עבודה זרה. He suggests that this too means the מצוה does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack works the same way as the שופר case. If a forbidden לולב does not work for the מצוה, then forbidden items are a problem for מצוות, against רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: The palm branch taken on סוכות
Taking the לולב to do the מצוה

phrases.english: A lulav of idol worship,
one should not take it.
Doesn't it mean,
that if he took it, he did not fulfill his obligation?

steps.triggerLanguage: לוּלָב שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה לֹא יִטּוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel challenge to step 18, using a different case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's rule that מצוות לאו ליהנות ניתנו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a forbidden לולב does not work for the מצוה, then forbidden items are a problem for מצוות.

steps.title: Same answer: the לולב counts after the fact
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the same answer: the ברייתא only means not at the start, but if he took it, he was יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means that if he took it, he was יוצא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the לולב case just like the שופר case. It is only a לכתחילה rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again, 'should not take' is read as 'don't do it at the start', not 'it doesn't count'. So רבא's rule still stands for now.

keyTerms.meaning: He took (the לולב)

phrases.english: No,
if he took it, he fulfilled his obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20, the same way step 19 answered step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source as לכתחילה only
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Should not take' means the מצוה does not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Should not take' only means not at the start; after the fact he is יוצא.

steps.title: A ברייתא says clearly that it does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that says openly: if he blew, he was not יוצא; if he took, he was not יוצא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught in a ברייתא: if he blew, he was not יוצא; if he took, he was not יוצא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the last two answers. A ברייתא says clearly that the מצוה does not count, even after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'only not at the start' answer no longer works, because this ברייתא speaks about after the fact and says לא יצא. Now it looks like a forbidden item cannot be used for a מצוה, which is a strong challenge to רבא.

phrases.english: But it was taught in a baraita:
if he blew, he did not fulfill his obligation;
if he took it, he did not fulfill his obligation!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: תָּקַע לֹא יָצָא, נָטַל לֹא יָצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answers of steps 19 and 21 and brings back the challenge to רבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The לכתחילה-only answers, and through them רבא's rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא says that even after the fact he is not יוצא, so a forbidden item seems to fail for a מצוה.

steps.title: רב אשי: Those cases cannot be compared
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to answer that the שופר and לולב cases are different from covering the blood; his reason continues in the next part.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: How can you compare? There...
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי begins to defend רבא by saying the שופר and לולב cases are not the same as covering blood. This line is only the opening; the actual reason continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'הכי השתא' he says the comparison is wrong. 'התם' points to the שופר and לולב cases, and the explanation of what makes them different comes right after this.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How can you compare?' Used to reject a comparison
'There', pointing to the case being compared

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
How can you compare?
There,
phrases.notes: He means the שופר and לולב of עבודה זרה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of step 22 by rejecting the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (continues beyond this section)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שופר and לולב cases prove that forbidden items fail for any מצוה, including כיסוי הדם.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שופר and לולב cases are different from כיסוי הדם; the reason comes next.
